content: I would put back screw in first, then the top 3. Back screw will make sure stop is flat against back. I had to force part down to get back screw in and once again had some layer separation. Glued layers together and put back screw in first and went together with no problem. Am I the only one with parts with low layer adhesion?
My lead screw is bumping against the back of the bed stopquite strongly so something is misaligned. Should I check the frame? The motor alignment? Anything else?

replies.content: I loosened the M3x10 that hold the Trapezoid nut to the Z plate.  There is a little adjustment to where those are positioned and you can use that to make the lead screw more vertical and hopefully not hit the bed stop.
The next step also brings the bed stop back slightly, so if it's touching the rod, that may fix it without adjustments to the rod.
